# glinet_led_schedule (Resource)

Manages the LED schedule of the router: on the scheduled days, the LEDs turn off at `turn_off_time` and on at `turn_on_time`. The router has one LED schedule, so use one instance of this resource. The schedule does not change `glinet_led`. The router keeps the times and days only from a write that enables the schedule. So when `enabled` is `false`, the provider first writes the schedule enabled with the configured times and days, and then disables it. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The LEDs are off from 22:00 to 07:00 on weekdays.
resource "glinet_led_schedule" "this" {
  enabled       = true
  turn_off_time = "22:00"
  turn_on_time  = "07:00"
  days          = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `days` (Set of Number) Days of the week when the schedule runs. Each day is a number from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday) (`week` in the router API).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is enabled (`enable` in the router API).
- `turn_off_time` (String) Time when the LEDs turn off (`turnoff_hour` and `turnoff_min` in the router API). Format `HH:MM`, 24 hours, in the time zone of the router.
- `turn_on_time` (String) Time when the LEDs turn on (`turnon_hour` and `turnon_min` in the router API). Format `HH:MM`, 24 hours, in the time zone of the router.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `led_schedule`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "led_schedule".
terraform import glinet_led_schedule.this led_schedule
```
